# ubuntu_ufw_rule Resource

Manages a ufw_rule resource via the hostsession.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "ubuntu_ufw_rule" "example" {
  target = var.host
  name = "allow-https"
  port = "443"
}
```
## Argument Reference

The resource supports the following arguments:

- `action` (Optional, Computed, string) - UFW action: allow, deny, reject, or limit. Defaults to allow.
- `allow_destructive_destroy` (Optional, bool) - Explicitly allow destructive destroy for protected or side-effecting host objects managed by this resource.
- `allow_ssh_disconnect` (Optional, Computed, bool) - Explicitly allow a rule change that would otherwise sever the current SSH access path.
- `direction` (Optional, Computed, string) - Traffic direction: in or out. Defaults to in.
- `ensure` (Optional, Computed, string) - Desired rule outcome (present or absent). Defaults to present.
- `from` (Optional, Computed, string) - Source CIDR, address, or the literal any. Defaults to any.
- `name` (Required, string) - Stable tf-nix name used to tag and reconcile the managed UFW rule.
- `port` (Required, string) - Single destination port or port range for the rule.
- `protocol` (Optional, Computed, string) - Transport protocol: tcp or udp. Defaults to tcp.
- `target` (Optional, string) - Target host or address for this resource. Overrides provider default_target.target.
- `target_port` (Optional, int64) - Target port for this resource. Overrides provider default_target.port.
- `to` (Optional, Computed, string) - Destination CIDR, address, or the literal any. Defaults to any.
- `transport` (Optional, string) - Transport for this resource. The current provider surface supports ssh.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes:

- `id` (string) - Unique identifier for this resource.
- `rule_comment` (string) - Computed managed UFW comment marker used to identify the rule on-host.
